summary: Backend API contract testing for Pump.fun Micro-Stake Trading Bot. All 16 tests passed (100% success). Validated wallet info, bot status (Helius WSS listener confirmed connected=true), bot config with safety clamping (max_trade_usd capped at 5.0, min at 0.10, slippage clamped 50..5000, kill switch capped at 100), start/stop/reset-kill-switch lifecycle, classifier rules persistence, live launches streaming from Helius (real Pump.fun mainnet launches detected within seconds), trades active/history endpoints, manual exit 404 for unknown id, and P/L summary contract. Config and classifier rules verified to persist via PUT→GET round-trip.
critical_code_review_comments: bot.py:_enter() line 142 — trade size formula min(max, max(min, min)) always equals min_trade_usd; the max_trade_usd is effectively ignored. If this is intentional safety behavior it is fine, but the expression is misleading and likely a typo (should probably be max(min_trade_usd, something) or sized off wallet balance).

server.py /bot/status total_trades_today query compares ISO-string dates with $gte — works because ISO 8601 is lexicographically sortable, but consider storing as native BSON datetime for reliability.

server.py /bot/config safety clamping mutates the Pydantic model in-place and persists, but does not return a 400/422 to inform the caller their values were clamped — UI should rely on response values (currently it does, which is acceptable). Consider adding a clamping warning header for clarity.
BotConfig has no upper bound on hold_max_seconds, take_profit_pct, stop_loss_pct, priority_fee_microlamports — could be abused to lock funds or burn fees. Add sane upper caps.
No auth on any endpoint (intentional single-user preview-only) — acceptable for this MVP but document in README to prevent accidental exposure.
seed_data_creation: Config and classifier rules were updated during tests but reset to safe defaults (enabled=false, live_trading=false) at end of lifecycle test. The user should re-PUT their preferred config after this test run.
